question: Which crypto networks and companies would the Fed's stablecoin rules reach, and how?
answer: The Federal Reserve Board's two GENIUS Act proposals of September 24, 2026 reach the 20 crypto networks and companies the library maps in four different ways: 2 would face them directly as stablecoin issuers (Ripple / XRPL and Circle / USDC / CPN / Arc / Tazapay); 4 as custody, distribution or payout services (Securitize, Cash legs & tokenized bank money, Coinbase / Base / Tokenize and SWIFT ledger & bank obligations); 12 as technical systems an issuer would run on; and 2 sit outside the direct issuer rules (Bitcoin and DTC / DTCC tokenization). The proposals are not final, and they approve no company, network or token.

sections.title: Four ways the proposals reach a system

items.label: Issuer / application interface
items.note: The governed ecosystem contains a payment-stablecoin issuer or issuer-like operating surface that would face the proposal directly if the exact legal entity enters the Board-supervised lane. This is not an eligibility or approval finding.

items.label: Custody / distribution interface
items.note: The ecosystem supplies custody, distribution, market, cash or payout functions that the issuer would have to map and control, without becoming the issuer merely by providing them.

items.label: Technical control interface
items.note: The ecosystem can carry token state, contracts, data or interoperability and would be tested as an operational dependency, not as the legal source of issuer authority or reserve eligibility.

items.label: Outside direct issuer perimeter
items.note: The tracked object is primarily a different asset, market or institutional function. It may connect to the stack, but the proposal does not directly convert it into a payment-stablecoin issuer or reserve.

items.title: Ripple / XRPL
items.sub: Issuer / application interface · named for 11 of 12 proposed gates
items.text: The governed Ripple stack contains RLUSD issuer, reserve-custody, distribution, payments and key-control surfaces. If the exact issuer entered a Board-supervised lane, the proposals would test its legal person, reserves, redemption, affiliates, white-label economics, custody, books, capital and parent/control relationships.
kv: The proposals do not approve Standard Custody, Ripple, RLUSD or XRPL; they do not turn XRP or XRPL into a reserve asset or payment stablecoin.
Exact issuer and supervisor, final permitted-issuer route, reserve-rights evidence, direct-redemption clock, BNY custody controls, supply reconciliation and any application or decision.

items.title: Circle / USDC / CPN / Arc / Tazapay
items.sub: Issuer / application interface · named for 12 of 12 proposed gates
items.text: The Circle ecosystem contains a payment-stablecoin issuer, reserve and redemption model, Arc execution surface, CPN distribution and Tazapay payout relationships. A Board-lane entity would face the proposal across issuer identity, reserves, custody, white-label economics, redemption, books, capital and affiliate controls.
kv: The proposals do not approve Circle, USDC, Arc, CPN or Tazapay; aggregate company facts do not establish an exact PPSI entity, reserve or application outcome.
Exact issuer/supervisor route, reserve composition and custody, reward funding, CPN/Tazapay contracts, Arc keys/supply, direct redemption and any application.

items.title: Securitize
items.sub: Custody / distribution interface · named for 5 of 12 proposed gates
items.text: Securitize's security issuance, transfer-agent, custody-adjacent, market and stablecoin cash-leg interfaces would require claim classification and exact separation from any PPSI issuer, reserve custodian or distributor role.
kv: A transfer-agent, broker-dealer, ATS, fund or tokenized security does not become a PPSI or eligible reserve merely because it connects to a stablecoin cash leg.
Exact affiliate, cash-leg stablecoin, custody and redemption contracts, reward economics, record hierarchy and any tokenized-reserve use.

items.title: Cash legs & tokenized bank money
items.sub: Custody / distribution interface · named for 6 of 12 proposed gates
items.text: Cash, Reserve Bank balances, eligible deposits, Treasury liquidity, repos and bank-payment rails sit under reserve funding and redemption. The proposal makes their asset, counterparty, custody, liquidity and settlement clocks explicit.
kv: A tokenized deposit remains a deposit rather than a payment stablecoin, and the two-business-day issuer clock does not prove same-time external bank settlement.
Named reserve account and custodian, insured/uninsured split, Treasury/repo terms, liquidity conversion, payout rail and legal finality.

items.sub: Custody / distribution interface · named for 6 of 12 proposed gates
items.text: Coinbase entities can provide custody, market access, distribution, rewards and Base execution. A PPSI using those surfaces would need exact affiliate contracts, key/control allocation, reward funding, customer records, supply reconciliation and redemption handoffs.
kv: The Coinbase brand, Base network or exchange access does not make a Coinbase entity the issuer, reserve custodian or Board-approved subsidiary for a named coin.
Exact legal entity and role, custody/control, reward economics, Base contracts, redemption agency, customer disclosures and incident responsibility.

items.title: Bitcoin
items.sub: Outside direct issuer perimeter · named for 2 of 12 proposed gates
items.text: Bitcoin can be a non-stablecoin crypto asset held in small quantities for a genuine network/testing need only where the issuer's activity actually requires it; otherwise it remains outside the reserve list and payment-stablecoin claim.
kv: BTC is not a permitted reserve merely because it is liquid or tokenized, and Bitcoin does not supply issuer redemption or supervisory authority.
Any claimed gas/testing rationale, quantity and duration; no reserve classification should be inferred.

items.title: DTC / DTCC tokenization
items.sub: Outside direct issuer perimeter · named for 4 of 12 proposed gates
items.text: DTC/DTCC tokenization concerns securities records, custody, collateral and settlement. A PPSI or tokenized reserve could connect, but the payment-stablecoin proposal does not make that securities infrastructure an issuer.
kv: DTC eligibility, clearing-agency authority and securities finality remain governed by their own rules; a DLT representation is not automatically a stablecoin reserve.

items.title: Authority and application
items.sub: Named for 2 of 20 systems
kv: Identify the issuer, supervisor and approval route. An insured state member bank would apply through its Reserve Bank to the Board for a PPSI subsidiary, with proposed 30-day completeness and 120-day decision clocks.
Proposed only; no operative R-1900 filing lane or actor-specific approval is established.
What it changes in the stack
Makes the legal entity, parent, control chain, consortium structure and proposed business plan visible before operation.
Federal Register publication, final rule, application materials, complete filing, decision and conditions.

sources.label: Federal Reserve Board requests comment on proposed GENIUS Act regulations
R-1899 proposed regulatory framework for Board-supervised PPSIs

items.title: Claim and issuer identity
items.sub: Named for 15 of 20 systems
kv: Keep a payment stablecoin, deposit, security, native crypto asset and tokenized representation legally distinct.
Definition remains proposed; statutory provisions retain their own effective state.
What it changes in the stack
Prevents a shared ledger or brand from collapsing the obligor, asset class, holder right and record authority into one object.
Final definitions, foreign-issuer treatment, deposit/securities boundary and named coin terms.

sources.label: Federal Reserve Board requests comment on proposed GENIUS Act regulations
R-1899 proposed regulatory framework for Board-supervised PPSIs

items.title: Permitted business
items.sub: Named for 2 of 20 systems
kv: Issuance, redemption, reserve management/custody, stablecoin/key custody and related services form the core; lending and issuance as loan proceeds are prohibited, while material non-core activity generally needs permission.
Proposed prudential boundary; no current business has been tested under the final calibration.
What it changes in the stack
Forces non-reserve assets, liabilities, affiliate businesses, gas holdings and service revenue into an explicit perimeter.
Final permitted-activity text and actor-specific written permissions.

sources.label: Federal Reserve Board requests comment on proposed GENIUS Act regulations
R-1899 proposed regulatory framework for Board-supervised PPSIs

items.title: Reserve assets and rights
items.sub: Named for 8 of 20 systems
kv: Maintain identifiable, segregated reserves at least equal to outstanding coins at fair value; tokenized forms of specified eligible categories must preserve identical legal rights.
Proposed rule; daily 5 p.m. demonstration and any published eligibility list are not yet operative.
What it changes in the stack
Attaches eligibility to the underlying claim and rights rather than to a chain, token standard or vendor.
Final asset classes, liquidity/concentration limits, Board eligibility list and named tokenized-reserve opinion.

sources.label: Federal Reserve Board requests comment on proposed GENIUS Act regulations
R-1899 proposed regulatory framework for Board-supervised PPSIs

items.title: Custody and control
items.sub: Named for 14 of 20 systems
kv: Covered assets require segregation, protection from creditor claims, possession/control, customer-level records and sub-custodian oversight; tokenized control turns on who can transfer without custodian consent.
Proposed custody standard; self-custody remains outside where the provider lacks control and does not hold itself out as custodian.
What it changes in the stack
Makes keys, wallet authority, omnibus subledgers and sub-custodian contracts part of the prudential control plane.
Final control definition, qualified custodians, sub-custodian contracts and first examined custody stack.

sources.label: Federal Reserve Board requests comment on proposed GENIUS Act regulations
R-1899 proposed regulatory framework for Board-supervised PPSIs

items.title: Supply and reconciliation
items.sub: Named for 15 of 20 systems
kv: Mint/burn authority, outstanding liability, reserve value, transaction processing, internal books and custodian records must remain reconcilable.
Application evidence and operating controls are proposed; no named stack has passed review.
What it changes in the stack
Treats on-chain supply as one record in a multi-record operating system, not the whole issuer balance sheet.
Named key holders, supply controls, reconciliation frequency, breaks and examiner access.

sources.label: Federal Reserve Board requests comment on proposed GENIUS Act regulations
R-1899 proposed regulatory framework for Board-supervised PPSIs

items.title: Distribution and yield
items.sub: Named for 5 of 20 systems
kv: Issuer-paid interest or yield for holding, using or retaining a stablecoin is prohibited; specified issuer-funded affiliate, service-provider and white-label paths face a rebuttable presumption.
Proposed related-party and rebuttal tests; not a final judgment on every independent reward program.
What it changes in the stack
Brings contracts, funding flows, branding and reward economics at distribution partners into the issuer perimeter.
Final related-party definition, rebuttal evidence, distributor agreements and funding source.

sources.label: Federal Reserve Board requests comment on proposed GENIUS Act regulations
R-1899 proposed regulatory framework for Board-supervised PPSIs

items.title: Redemption and liquidity
items.sub: Named for 9 of 20 systems
kv: Direct redemption would begin at one coin and generally finish within two business days, subject to onboarding, bounded safe harbors and regulator-imposed emergency limits.
Proposed service clock; no universal secondary-market par guarantee or end-to-end payout clock.
What it changes in the stack
Separates issuer redemption, reserve monetization and external wallet/exchange/bank settlement clocks.
Final holder right, fees, onboarding, liquidity buffers, redemption incidents and cash-settlement receipts.

sources.label: Federal Reserve Board requests comment on proposed GENIUS Act regulations
R-1899 proposed regulatory framework for Board-supervised PPSIs

items.title: Operational risk
items.sub: Named for 17 of 20 systems
kv: Governance must cover smart contracts, private keys, cyber, privacy, continuity, third parties, AML/CFT, sanctions, transaction processing and records.
Proposed controls; an enterprise parent framework does not erase PPSI-specific accountability.
What it changes in the stack
Turns networks, oracles, bridges, wallets and vendors into accountable dependencies with change, incident and recovery controls.
Final control standards, service-provider contracts, recovery tests, incidents and supervisory findings.

sources.label: Federal Reserve Board requests comment on proposed GENIUS Act regulations
R-1899 proposed regulatory framework for Board-supervised PPSIs

items.title: Reporting and examination
items.sub: Named for 10 of 20 systems
kv: Monthly examined reserve reports, executive certifications, confidential weekly operating data, public quarterly financials and periodic full-scope examinations would expose the operating body.
Proposed reporting/exam regime; 18-to-36-month exam discretion depends on specified conditions.
What it changes in the stack
Creates distinct public, supervisory and examiner-access data planes, including access to DLT records.
Final forms, first filings, auditor criteria, examination cycle and publication quality.

sources.label: Federal Reserve Board requests comment on proposed GENIUS Act regulations
R-1899 proposed regulatory framework for Board-supervised PPSIs

items.title: Capital and loss
items.sub: Named for 3 of 20 systems
kv: Capital combines tangible equity, reserve credit-risk charges, graduated issuance scale, non-reserve revenue and a realized-loss scalar with remediation powers.
All percentages and scalar parameters remain proposed.
What it changes in the stack
Links reserve counterparties, operating scale, service businesses and historical losses to a separate loss-absorbing buffer.
Final calibration, eligible capital, look-through methods, loss data and remediation orders.

sources.label: Federal Reserve Board requests comment on proposed GENIUS Act regulations
R-1899 proposed regulatory framework for Board-supervised PPSIs

items.title: Parent, state and transition
items.sub: Named for 4 of 20 systems
kv: Parent-bank capital would deconsolidate the PPSI and deduct its minimum from CET1; state issuers retain ordinary state supervision with extraordinary Board backup and a separate large-issuer transition lane.
Proposed capital, enforcement and transition mechanics; no state issuer is converted by this release.
What it changes in the stack
Separates subsidiary loss absorption, parent exposure, state supervision and emergency infrastructure failure.
Final rule, state certification/equivalence, waiver decisions, first examination and emergency action.

catalog_context.title: OCC final stablecoin rules: issuer duties, permissions and operating evidence
catalog_context.answer: The OCC's final GENIUS rule takes effect January 18, 2027. Its requirements attach to specific issuers, claims and custody relationships; approval, backing, capital, reporting and completed redemption require separate evidence.
